subject: Usage health review — ROI tranche & canary rollout proposal
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lambert <sophie@lyra-analytics.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@lyra-analytics.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Usage health review — ROI tranche & canary rollout proposal

Hi Sophie / Tom,

Thanks again for running the workshop yesterday — good conversation on latency and token mix. I pulled together the Q2 usage export and a short ROI snapshot (attached). High-level observations: 

- Tokens are spiking during peak inference windows (14:00-16:00 ET) with a 22% tail in long-context requests (>1k tokens).
- Prefix cache hit is ~18% on your assistant flows; that’s a clear opportunity for per-route caching.
- Average p95 latency on the standard model is 320ms; with quantized dedicated variants we can bring that to ~200–230ms for the same throughput.

Proposal / ask:
1) Pilot a 6-week canary on Dedicated with an initial reserved tranche (50k tokens/day equivalent) and burst allowance for 30 days to smooth adoption.
2) Run a short latency-led A/B for your top two routes (assistant vs. summarization) to compare quantized vs. full-fp models.
3) If pilot meets the latency and cost targets, roll a term extension: 12-months with a 10% committed discount in exchange for the reserved tranche and a capped burst budget.

Next steps: if Tuesday morning works I’ll send a one-page plan and updated pricing. I’ve attached usage_report_q2.csv — please flag anything missing.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Sophie Lambert <sophie@lyra-analytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@lyra-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Usage health review — ROI tranche & canary rollout proposal

Rachel — thanks, this is helpful. Quick clarifications: 

1) Can you break out the token mix by environment (staging vs. prod)? Our engineering team wants to understand how much of the peak is noise.
2) For the pilot tranche you mention — is the burst allowance billed separately or built into the reserved price?

We’re open to the 6-week canary but need a clear success metric for both latency and cost (e.g., p95 <= 250ms and cost per 1k tokens <= $X).

I’ll bring this to Tom and we can triage internally — Tuesday morning is doable.

— Sophie
Sophie Lambert
Head of Platform Engineering
Lyra Analytics
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lambert <sophie@lyra-analytics.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@lyra-analytics.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Usage health review — ROI tranche & canary rollout proposal

Sophie — good questions. Answers below and I’ve attached a sample of raw latency traces (latency_samples.zip) for your infra team.

1) Token mix by environment: the attached CSV has an env column — prod accounts for ~86% of the peak traffic. Staging traffic is <5% in the high-window, so noise is limited.

2) Billing for burst: we recommend including a capped burst allowance in the reserved tranche (e.g., 25% of reserved/day for the first 30 days) and any additional burst used beyond that would be billed at an overage rate. We’ll state exact numbers in the one-page plan.

Suggested success metrics for the pilot: 
- p95 latency on the primary assistant route <= 250ms for 90% of days in the pilot period.
- Per-1k token cost reduction >= 18% against current baseline when using the quantized variant + batching.
- No more than 2 production incidents attributable to model runtime during pilot.

Tuesday 10:00 AM ET works for a 30-minute cadence sync to agree the canary controls and pricing. I’ll circulate a one-pager beforehand.

Thanks,
Rachel
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Lambert <sophie@lyra-analytics.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@lyra-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-06-03T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Usage health review — ROI tranche & canary rollout proposal

Rachel / team — looping in pricing and ops notes from my side. A couple of practical guardrails we should include in the canary doc: 

- Canary routing: start with 5% traffic routing for week 1, 20% week 2–3, then 50% if metrics hold. Auto-fallback to hosted model on spike.
- SLA credit carveout: include a 1-week remediation window before crediting; avoid immediate credits for pilot.
- Price framing: propose a 10% committed discount on the reserved tranche with an overage of 1.8x list for additional burst after the capped allowance.

I’ll draft a short pricing table and share in the Drive link Rachel referenced. If Lyra confirms the success metrics we should be able to convert pilot to a term amendment (12 months) with the discount baked in.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Director, Renewals
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@lyra-analytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Lambert <sophie@lyra-analytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-04T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Usage health review — ROI tranche & canary rollout proposal

Thanks all. Lyra is comfortable proceeding with a pilot under those guardrails — we just need a one-page SOW + an estimate for the reserved tranche and burst ceiling.

Action items for Redwood:
- Provide one-page SOW (scope, success metrics, timeline).
- Provide pricing table for reserved tranche + burst terms (Jordan to own).
- Share Drive link to the proposal and HubSpot deal id for procurement.

We’d also like a 30-day burst trial (no charge) for the initial ramp if possible — that will help our platform team validate behavior without immediate overage risk. If you can accommodate that, procurement is ready to issue a PO the week after the pilot kickoff.

— Tom
VP, Business Operations
Lyra Analytics
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@lyra-analytics.com>, Sophie Lambert <sophie@lyra-analytics.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-07T17:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Usage health review — ROI tranche & canary rollout proposal

Tom / Sophie — great. Confirming next steps and owners: 

1) Rachel -> Circulate one-page SOW (today EOD). Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3driveProposal
2) Jordan -> Pricing table + draft term amendment (by 2027-06-09). HubSpot deal id HS-54219 (DEAL-2027-0421).
3) Sean -> Ops playbook and routing controls; will include auto-fallback and monitoring checklist.

On the 30-day burst trial: we can include a one-time 30-day burst allowance during the initial ramp at no charge (cap to be defined in the SOW). We’ll mark any usage above that cap as billable at the overage rate.

Attaching the two artifacts we referenced (usage_report_q2.csv, latency_samples.zip). I’ll drop the SOW in Drive and ping you when it’s live.

Thanks everyone — will follow up with the final SOW and calendar invite for Tuesday 10am ET.
